figures.finding: Heard Island and McDonald Islands have no actors' agreement, guild or fund: they are an uninhabited Australian external territory managed by the Australian Antarctic Division.
figures.applies: Heard Island and McDonald Islands (HM), as of 2026-11-01; any work there would be engaged from Australia (AU market files), not modeled further.

sources.said: The islands are an Australian External Territory and enjoy World Heritage protection and marine reserve status. They are managed by the Australian Antarctic Division (AAD). Heard Island and McDonald Islands are unoccupied by humans and remain largely undisturbed by human activity.

blockers.sought: The stage actor's minimum: an agreement, a rate card or a statutory rule setting a stage actor's pay, or a source saying none does.

tried.web-search: 1 WebSearch (standard): 'Heard Island and McDonald Islands filming permit entry Environment Protection and Management Ordinance 1987 Australian Antarctic Division' (the stage actor's minimum, the methods round of 2026-11-04). Result: led to the AAD's territory-legislation and permit pages, legislation.gov.au copies of the HIMI ordinances, the HIMI environmental approval form and ABLIS's 'Permit to Enter and Carry out a Specified Activity on Heard or McDonald Island'; filming is not named as an activity; no broadcaster, theatre, fund, pay or fee
tried.institution: The Australian Antarctic Division's own page: www.antarctica.gov.au/antarctic-operations/stations-and-field-locations/heard-island/protection-and-management/legislation/territory-legislation/ (saved l4t/files/m17/hm-aad-terrleg.html, sha256 ea35455586e67bee762f9b069617065390959b898978779972a082e8ae046c92) (the stage actor's minimum, the methods round of 2026-11-04). Result: read: the laws that apply are the HIMI Act 1953, the Environment Protection and Management Ordinance 1987 (a permit to enter the Territory, and a permit for activities that may harm its environment), the Criminal Procedures Ordinance 1993 and the Weapons Ordinance 2001, plus Commonwealth laws expressly applied and 'The laws, other than criminal laws, in force from time to time in the Australian Capital Territory in so far as they are applicable'. No production incentive, fund, broadcaster, theatre or pay rule of the Territory's own
tried.official-register: Federal Register of Legislation: the HIMI Act 1953 (C1953A00007), latest compilation (www.legislation.gov.au/C1953A00007/latest/text, hm-act1953.html, 7e41500d…) and its text (…/C1953A00007/2008-07-04/2008-07-04/text/original/epub/OEBPS/document_1/document_1.html, l4t/files/m17/hm-act1953-doc.html, sha256 31beb008224aa8fef69fc181ad891c713a0a897cf5e9f29ca8f529edf3a04668), s. 5 read (the stage actor's minimum, the methods round of 2026-11-04). Result: read: s. 5(1) 'the laws (other than the criminal laws) in force from time to time in the Australian Capital Territory ... are, by virtue of this section, so far as applicable to the Territory and not inconsistent with an Ordinance, in force in the Territory as if the Territory formed part of the Australian Capital Territory'; s. 7 applies Commonwealth Acts that say so. So whatever production incentive, fund or stage rate binds there is Australia's (the ACT's and the Commonwealth's): the Territory has none of its own, and no resident trade to use one
